definition: The amount of factual knowledge a model can store in its parameters, commonly estimated at roughly two bits per parameter.
details: Rather than judging a model by loss or benchmark scores, knowledge capacity counts the bits of factual tuples — such as (USA, capital, Washington D.C.) — that the weights can hold. Controlled studies estimate a ceiling of about 2 bits per parameter even at int8 quantization, which implies a 7B model can store on the order of 14B bits of knowledge, more than the English Wikipedia and textbooks combined. The measure is useful for comparing designs: training duration, quantization, sparsity constraints such as mixture-of-experts, and the signal-to-noise ratio of the training data all change how much of that capacity is actually used. It also helps explain how parameter count (stored knowledge) can be decoupled from per-token compute.
